note: DECLARED ROUTING for individual questions of Hannetjie's, applied by map-criteria.mjs AFTER the rule table. Read the header comment in that file before adding an entry. Every entry is checked at build time: the quiz+n must address exactly one harvested card, `was` must still be the opening of that card's question, and each of `crit`/`add`/`drop` must actually change something. An entry that stops biting fails the build rather than sitting here looking useful.

kinds.topic: the browse tab the card appears under, applied by harvest.mjs (not by map-criteria.mjs, which owns crit/add/drop). Quiz-level routing gets the body system right but not always the tab. Declaring it here overrides the rule tables for one question, and the same contract applies: the entry must change something or the harvest fails.
kinds.add: the rules left this card with NO focus point, and no rule could reach it — the question names no physiology because the physiology is in the image. Listing the crit here is the only honest alternative to a rule loose enough to catch it by accident.
kinds.crit: the rules found the right SET of focus points but the wrong one is first. Primary is otherwise decided by the order of the rule table, which is alphabetical-ish accident, and `crit` is what the reader is told the card is about — and what Ring 0 deals. The named id must already be among the rule hits (or be added by this same entry).
kinds.drop: a rule fired on a word this card only mentions in passing. Removing it here keeps the rule general for the cards it is right about.

routes.quiz: Practice Lab 2: SAQ & MC Quiz (10 marks)
routes.was: The structure labelled at B is a
routes.why: A cross-section of the trachea with B on the cartilage; the options are four ways of describing a tracheal cartilage ring. Nothing in the words says trachea — the image does. resp-2 is the criterion that names the trachea.

routes.quiz: Practice Lab 2: SAQ & MC Quiz (10 marks)
routes.was: The white shiny part of this structure labelled at A (in the first image) and 1 (in the second image) is made from?
routes.why: A dissection photograph: A points at the white glistening wall of the airway, and the answer is that it is collagen. Same structure as Question 4 of this quiz, which asks what the tube is (the trachea). resp-2 covers the trachea and the bronchial tree.

routes.quiz: Practice Lab 1: SAQ & MC Quiz (20 marks)
routes.was: Complete the passage. (Practice Lab 1)
routes.why: The stem is a Canvas group title. The question itself is an image of the heart's surface — what is the white tissue on it (adipose) and what does it do (mechanical cushion) — which is criterion 5.2, the coverings of the heart.

routes.quiz: MODULE 1.2: RESP BASIC ANATOMY (10 Marks)
routes.was: Find and describe at least ONE error in the labelling of the AI created summary below and describe it in the answer space.
routes.why: The summary being marked is a diagram of the airway split into conducting and respiratory zones, and the errors to find are where that boundary is drawn and which structures carry cartilage. That is resp-3 — differentiate the organs of the conducting and respiratory zones — and it is the only card in the pack whose subject IS that boundary.

routes.quiz: MODULE 1.1: CVS4 BLOOD PRESSURE (10 marks)
routes.was: Of the following cardiovascular components, which contains the majority of the body’s blood volume at any one time?
routes.why: Veins and venules hold roughly two thirds of the blood — the capacitance property that separates a vein from an artery. cvs-2 is the criterion asking for the functional differences between artery, vein and capillary. Her CVS4 deck calls them the blood “reservoir” vessels, but it does so inside the vasomotor reflex, and the question here asks the plain anatomy, not the reflex.

routes.quiz: MODULE 1.2: (SAQ &MC) STUDENT MARKED: RESPIRATORY PRACTICE TEST (20 marks)
routes.was: External respiration is affected by all the following except
routes.why: The question names external respiration and asks which factor does not affect it. It was filed under resp-5 because three of its four options are respiratory-membrane words — the card was being described by its distractors. resp-9 is the criterion for external respiration and the factors affecting gas exchange, and this is the question that asks it.

routes.quiz: MODULE 1.2: RESPIRATORY SYSTEM GAS LAWS (20 marks)
routes.was: External respiration is affected by all of the following factors except:
routes.why: The same question, set again in a second quiz with the wording changed — the strongest evidence signal in the pack. Same reasoning as the Respiratory Practice Test entry above.

routes.quiz: Respiratory System: Terminology Assessment
routes.was: Complete the passage. (Respiratory System)
routes.why: Ten blanks, each one a respiratory term to name from its definition — dyspnoea, pneumothorax, atelectasis, eupnoea, cyanosis. It is the terminology assessment, and resp-17 is the terminology criterion. It was filed under resp-2 because the definitions name the airways they happen to be about.

routes.quiz: MODULE 1.3: QUIZ: DISEASES / TERMINOLOGY RELATED TO THE LYMPHATIC SYSTEM
routes.was: Answer the question to ensure that the conditions and their descriptions match. Help is just a click away.
routes.why: Lymphoedema, sentinel nodes, Hodgkin's disease, splenectomy — this is criterion lymph-4's own list, from the quiz named after it. It was filed under cvs-3, capillary fluid movement, because `oedema` sits inside `lymphoedema` and cvs-3 is declared earlier in the rule table. That single accident is why the lymphatic terminology point had no card of its own.

routes.quiz: MODULE 1.1: CVS HOMEOSTASIS (30 Marks)
routes.was: Complete the passage. (MODULE 1.1)
routes.why: The hardest of these to call, and the reasoning is worth keeping. The passage opens as criterion 11 word for word — the effects of venous return, plasma electrolytes, stress and exercise on cardiac functions — and its first six blanks are that. Its last four are not: they ask what exercise does to cardiac activity and to peripheral resistance in a fit person, and every section of the passage closes on blood pressure. That is criterion 13, how blood pressure is affected by stress and exercise, and this is the only card in the pack that TESTS it rather than assuming it. cvs-11 stays on the card; it was never primary here anyway — the rules had filed the whole thing under cvs-3, capillary fluid movement, on the word osmolality.

routes.quiz: MODULE 1.1: CVS4 BLOOD PRESSURE (10 marks)
routes.was: Chemical factors that contribute to increased blood pressure are
routes.why: Six chemicals to sort by whether they raise blood pressure — aldosterone, angiotensin II and adrenaline yes; histamine, nitric oxide and atrial natriuretic peptide no. cvs-5 fires on the word `Atrial` inside ATRIAL natriuretic peptide, so a chemical-control-of-BP question was being led by the functional anatomy of the heart. Found by reading the 11 Aug answer keys, not by any count. cvs-12 is the criterion and is already on the card.

routes.quiz: MODULE 1.1: CVS HOMEOSTASIS (30 Marks)
routes.was: Complete the passage. (MODULE 1.1)
routes.why: Seven blanks: the conduction pathway, then the nerves, hormones and electrolytes that speed the heart up or slow it down. That is criterion 9 — the homeostatic control of heart rate, neural and hormonal — almost sentence for sentence. It was filed under cvs-5, functional anatomy of the heart, on the word `myocardium`, and cvs-5 has 78 other cards to lead with.

routes.quiz: MODULE 1: SAQ & MC: FORMATIVE CVS, LYMPHATIC & RESPIRATORY SYSTEMS *(50 marks)
routes.was: Complete the passage. (MODULE 1)
routes.why: Lagi's blood pressure is 150/90 and his heart rate is 110: this is the blood-pressure case study, and it is the biggest single question in her 50-mark formative. It was filed under cvs-2 because a micrograph of an artery and a vein is one of its ten blanks — a case study being named after one of its parts.

routes.quiz: Respiratory (SAQ & MC) Pre-Lab Quiz
routes.was: Select from the following which factors directly influence a persons lung capacity
routes.why: Eight true/false factors, every one of them about lung capacity — height, sex, smoking, age. cvs-10 fired on `age`, which is on its own list of general factors affecting heart rate, and because cvs-10 is declared first it became this card's focus point: a lung-volume question standing at the head of “General factors affecting HR, SV and CO”, which is what Ring 0 would have dealt for that point. resp-6 is the criterion for lung volumes and capacities.

routes.quiz: MODULE 1: SAQ & MC: FORMATIVE CVS, LYMPHATIC & RESPIRATORY SYSTEMS *(50 marks)
routes.was: Complete the passage. (MODULE 1)
routes.why: Ten blanks on mesenteric adenitis, the MALT system, which cells are in lymph and where lymph drains. Its focus point was cvs-3 — capillary fluid movement — because `lymphoedema` is one of the drop-down options and `edema` was matching inside it. lymph-2 is the functional anatomy of the lymphatic system, which is what ten of the ten blanks are asking about.

routes.quiz: MODULE 1.1: SAQ & MC: CVS REVIEW *(35 marks )
routes.was: Describe the difference in normal BP (mean) in the arteries, arterioles, capillaries and venae cavae?
routes.why: cvs-2 fires on "difference in normal BP … in the arteries, arterioles, capillaries", which is the pressure gradient down the tree — cvs-4, and the card already carries it. Naming three vessel types in a row is not the same as being asked how their walls differ.

routes.quiz: MODULE 1.1: THE CVS: HEART ANATOMY (40 marks)
routes.was: Match the following terms to their definitions:
routes.why: Definitions of blood pressure, systolic pressure, stroke volume and cardiac output. cvs-2 fires on the phrase inside one of them — "the force of blood against the walls of the arteries" — which is the definition of BP, not a claim about artery structure.

routes.quiz: Practice Lab 1: SAQ & MC Quiz (20 marks)
routes.was: Patient A had a Myocardial Infarction due to the total occlusion of the Left Anterior Descending coronary artery.
routes.why: cvs-2 fires on "what parts of the heart wall are perfused by the Left Anterior Descending coronary artery". The heart wall is not a vessel wall; this card is coronary circulation and it already carries cvs-5 and cvs-6.

routes.quiz: MODULE 1.1 SHOCK QUIZ (5 Marks)
routes.was: Cold and clammy skin, tachycardia, and rapid breathing are clinical
routes.why: The stem is the presentation of shock and the key is the sympathetic response to it. cvs-12 was chosen by the word "Renin" in a distractor — long-term renal BP control is not what this question tests.

routes.quiz: MODULE 1.1 SHOCK QUIZ (5 Marks)
routes.was: A trauma patient is progressing rapidly into circulatory shock. He is
routes.why: A shock-classification question: the true statements are a ruptured mesenteric artery and loss of sympathetic tone. cvs-5 was chosen by "Myocardial infarction" in a distractor.

routes.quiz: MODULE 1.1: CVS3 CARDIAC CONDUCTION & ECG (10 marks)
routes.was: Exercise ....
routes.why: The stem is "Exercise ...." and the key is that venous return rises and stroke volume with it — cvs-11 is the focus point that names venous return and exercise. cvs-5 was chosen by "ventricle" in a distractor.

routes.quiz: MODULE 1.2: (SAQ &MC) STUDENT MARKED: RESPIRATORY PRACTICE TEST (20 marks)
routes.was: The rate of carbon dioxide and oxygen exchange is roughly the same, despite
routes.why: Why CO2 and O2 exchange at similar rates despite different gradients is a question about the factors governing external respiration — solubility. The only rule that reached this card fired on "respiratory membrane" in a distractor.

routes.quiz: MODULE 1.2: (SAQ &MC) STUDENT MARKED: RESPIRATORY PRACTICE TEST (20 marks)
routes.was: Which of the following is NOT a factor that promotes oxygen dissociation from
routes.why: What promotes oxygen release from haemoglobin is oxygen transport. resp-8 (atmospheric vs alveolar air) was chosen by "partial pressure" in a distractor.

routes.quiz: MODULE 1.2: RESP BASIC ANATOMY (10 Marks)
routes.was: What is the potential space between the two lungs called?
routes.why: The mediastinum is thoracic and respiratory anatomy. cvs-5 was chosen by "pericardium" in a distractor — the question is not about the heart.

routes.quiz: MODULE 1.2: RESP BASIC ANATOMY (10 Marks)
routes.was: The membrane that forms the shiny layer on the lung surface is known as the
routes.why: The key is visceral pleura. cvs-5 was chosen by "epicardium" in a distractor.

routes.quiz: MODULE 1.2: RESP BASIC ANATOMY (10 Marks)
routes.was: The double membrane that surrounds the lung is known as the ............ .
routes.why: The key is the three pleural layers. cvs-5 was chosen by "epicardium" in a distractor.

routes.quiz: MODULE 1.2: RESP BASIC ANATOMY (10 Marks)
routes.was: Emphysema is a condition that causes the ____________________ to loose
routes.why: The key is alveoli — the question tests that alveolar tissue supplies elastic recoil. resp-2 was chosen by "bronchi" in a distractor.

routes.quiz: MODULE 1.2: RESPIRATORY SYSTEM BASIC PHYSIOLOGY (15 marks)
routes.was: The pressure in the alveoli is known as __________.
routes.why: Intrapulmonary pressure is a ventilation-mechanics pressure. resp-2 was chosen by "pleura" in a distractor.

routes.quiz: MODULE 1.2: RESPIRATORY SYSTEM BASIC PHYSIOLOGY (15 marks)
routes.was: Air is forced out of the lungs during normal expiration due to _________.
routes.why: Elastic recoil driving passive expiration is ventilation mechanics. resp-2 was chosen by "bronchi" in a distractor.

routes.quiz: MODULE 1.2: RESPIRATORY SYSTEM BASIC PHYSIOLOGY (15 marks)
routes.was: The pressure exerted by each gas in a mixture is proportional to its
routes.why: Dalton’s law of partial pressures belongs with the composition of atmospheric versus alveolar air. resp-7 was chosen by "Boyle" in a distractor.

routes.was: Why is the rate of CO 2 exchange roughly equivalent to that of O 2 despite
routes.why: Same question as the practice test: solubility as a factor in external respiration. The only rule that reached it fired on "respiratory membrane" in a distractor.

routes.quiz: MODULE 1.2: RESPIRATORY SYSTEM BASIC PHYSIOLOGY (15 marks)

routes.why: A gas-law question. cvs-11 was chosen by "Frank-Starling" in a distractor — a cardiac law that is here only as a wrong answer.

routes.why: The key is surfactant lowering surface tension — the alveolar focus point names surfactant explicitly. resp-2 was chosen by "trachea" in a distractor.

routes.quiz: MODULE 1.3: QUIZ: DISEASES / TERMINOLOGY RELATED TO THE LYMPHATIC SYSTEM
routes.was: The linked article would help. Which of the following is NOT a function of
routes.why: The stem asks which option is NOT a function of the lymphatic system, which is lymph-1 exactly. cvs-3 was chosen by "filtration of tissue fluid" in a distractor.

routes.quiz: Practice Lab 1: SAQ & MC Quiz (20 marks)
routes.was: What is the vein labelled A
routes.why: Every option is a named arm or shoulder vein and the key is the subclavian vein; this is venous anatomy from a cardiovascular practice lab. lymph-2 was the only rule hit, and it fired because the thoracic duct drains into the subclavian vein — a fact this question never raises.

routes.quiz: MODULE 1.1: CVS4 BLOOD PRESSURE (10 marks)
routes.was: The heart rate in a trained athlete is lower than in untrained individuals.
routes.why: A resting-heart-rate question — it belongs with cardiac output, not with blood pressure control, which is where the quiz-level rule puts everything in this quiz.

routes.quiz: MODULE 1.1: CVS4 BLOOD PRESSURE (10 marks)
routes.was: What kind of a blood system do humans have?
routes.why: Closed and double circulation is heart-and-circuit anatomy; the quiz-level rule files this whole quiz under blood pressure control.

routes.quiz: MODULE 1.1: THE CVS: HEART ANATOMY (40 marks)
routes.was: Mix and match
routes.why: Hypertension, hypotension and orthostatic hypotension are blood-pressure terms; the quiz-level rule files this whole quiz under heart anatomy.

routes.quiz: MODULE 1.1: THE CVS: HEART ANATOMY (40 marks)
routes.was: Which formula shows the relationship between BP, CO & SVR
routes.why: BP = CO × SVR is the blood pressure relationship; the quiz-level rule files this whole quiz under heart anatomy.

routes.quiz: MODULE 1.1: THE CVS: HEART ANATOMY (40 marks)
routes.was: Match the causes of edema and the mechanisms:
routes.why: Causes of oedema are capillary fluid dynamics; the quiz-level rule files this whole quiz under heart anatomy.

routes.quiz: MODULE 1.2: AIRWAYS, BARO- & CHEMORECEPTORS (10 marks)
routes.was: Which statement is false regarding the Carina. The carina is......
routes.why: The carina and the cough reflex are the pathway-of-air focus point, which names both. resp-2 was chosen by "trachea" in a distractor.

routes.quiz: MODULE 1.2: AIRWAYS, BARO- & CHEMORECEPTORS (10 marks)
routes.was: You cannot kill yourself by holding your breath since the chemoreceptors in
routes.why: Chemoreceptors driving the urge to breathe. The keyword table put it in Vessels & fluid dynamics because the stem says "carotid artery".

routes.quiz: MODULE 1.3:SAQ & MC: FLUID, ELECTROLYTE & FLUID BALANCE (10 marks)
routes.was: The typical fluid replacement for the patient with an intracellular fluid volume deficit is:
routes.why: Which IV fluid to give for an intracellular deficit — the key is isotonic. lymph-1 was the ONLY rule that reached this card, and it fired on "fluid volume" inside "fluid volume deficit": a nursing term for dehydration, not one of the lymphatic system's functions. cvs-3 does not match by rule either, so it is added here. It is the focus point this pack already uses for tonicity and osmolality — Question 1 of this same quiz, on plasma osmolality against the inside of a red cell, sits there — and no focus point in the 38 is about fluid and electrolyte balance as such.
